items.stem: A projection shows revenue growing 50% while receivables grow 200%. What is the most likely analytical concern?

options.text: Deteriorating collections or aggressive revenue recognition
options.rationale: Correct: receivables outpacing revenue can signal slow collections or revenue quality issues.
High receivable growth is not a measure of excess profitability.
Depreciation is unrelated to receivables growing faster than revenue.

options.text: Nothing; the two always move together one-for-one
options.rationale: They need not move proportionally; the divergence is the signal.

items.explanation: Correct: receivables outpacing revenue can signal slow collections or revenue quality issues.

items.stem: Sensitivity analysis differs from scenario analysis primarily because sensitivity analysis:

options.text: Changes one input at a time to see its isolated effect
options.rationale: Correct: sensitivity analysis varies a single driver while holding others constant.
That would be one specific scenario, not sensitivity analysis.

options.text: Requires at least ten simultaneous input changes
options.rationale: That is closer to scenario or Monte Carlo analysis.
Sensitivity analysis is measured relative to a base case.

items.explanation: Correct: sensitivity analysis varies a single driver while holding others constant.

items.stem: Select TWO practices that improve the credibility of a financial projection presented to executives.

options.text: Clearly stating the key assumptions behind the numbers
options.rationale: Correct: transparent assumptions let reviewers judge the projection.

options.text: Showing a downside and an upside case
options.rationale: Correct: presenting a range communicates uncertainty honestly.

options.text: Reporting figures to eight decimal places for precision
options.rationale: False precision does not improve credibility and can mislead.

options.text: Hiding the model so it cannot be questioned
Using a different definition of profit on every slide
options.rationale: Inconsistent definitions undermine trust in the analysis.

items.explanation: Correct: transparent assumptions let reviewers judge the projection.
